title: Lateral sclerosis in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is an upper motor neuron distal axonopathy (“dying back”): a clinical-neuropathological study
title_zh: 肌萎缩侧索硬化症侧向硬化为上运动神经元远端轴突病变（“退化回退”）：临床-神经病理学研究
abstract: Abstract The hallmark neuropathological feature of upper motor neuron (UMN) degeneration in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is the “sclerosis” of the lateral corticospinal tract (CST)—the major axonal pathway connecting UMNs to lower motor neurons (LMNs). However, few studies since Charcot’s original descriptions in the nineteenth century have directly correlated clinical UMN phenotypes with corresponding neuropathological findings. We examined the pathology of the lateral CST at the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar levels of the spinal cord from ALS patients with predominantly UMN (UMN-p) phenotypes and compared it with that in patients with predominantly LMN (LMN-p) phenotypes. We assessed myelin loss, axonal degeneration, neuroinflammation, and TDP-43 pathology. Spinal cords from UMN-p ALS cases exhibited pronounced myelin loss in the lateral CST compared to LMN-p cases and controls, consistent with clinical phenotyping. Quantitative analysis revealed significant axonal loss across all axon diameter ranges in UMN-p ALS, which was more severe than in LMN-p ALS. Importantly, axonal loss was more pronounced in the lumbar than in the cervical spinal cord. We identified a distinct population of foamy, inflammatory microglia localized to regions of severe myelin and axonal loss in UMN-p ALS. TDP-43 was measurably increased in the UMN axons of the lateral and ventral CSTs. In summary, “lateral sclerosis” of ALS correlates to clinically imputed UMN degeneration. It consists of a combination of myelin loss, distal greater than proximal axonal degeneration, inflammatory microglial activation within the CSTs, and abnormally increased axonal TDP-43. The length-dependent gradient of motor axonal loss supports a "dying-back" process. A detailed comparison of “dying-forward” and “dying-forward” is provided in the Discussion. The association of loss of axons and myelin with abnormal microglial activity shows glio-axonal interactions in UMN axon degeneration, the latter CST (lateral sclerosis) across all three spinal cord levels in the ALS UMN-p samples but does not establish a causal relationship.
abstract_zh: 摘要 上运动神经元（UMN）在肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）中退化的标志性神经病理特征是侧向皮质脊髓束（CST）的“硬化”——连接UMN与下运动神经元（LMN）的主要轴突通路。然而，自19世纪Charcot最初描述以来，少有研究直接将临床UMN表型与相应的神经病理发现相关联。我们检查了ALS患者在颈、胸、腰段脊髓侧向CST的病理，并与主要为LMN表型的患者进行比较。我们评估了髓鞘丢失、轴突退化、神经炎症和TDP-43病理。UMN主导型ALS病例的脊髓在侧向CST中表现出显著的髓鞘丢失，明显高于LMN主导型病例和对照组，符合临床表型。定量分析显示UMN主导型ALS在所有轴突直径范围内均显著轴突丢失，且比LMN主导型ALS更严重。值得注意的是，轴突丢失在腰段脊髓中比颈段更为明显。我们在UMN主导型ALS中识别出一群富含泡沫、炎性微胶质细胞，局限于严重髓鞘和轴突丢失的区域。TDP-43在侧向和腹侧CST的UMN轴突中明显升高。总之，ALS的“侧向硬化”与临床推断的UMN退化相关。它由髓鞘丢失、远端大于近端轴突退化、CST内炎性微胶质细胞激活以及轴突TDP-43异常升高组成。运动轴突丢失的长度梯度支持“退化回退”过程。讨论中提供了“前向退化”和“后向退化”的详细比较。轴突和髓鞘丢失与异常微胶质细胞活性之间的关联显示了UMN轴突退化中的胶质-轴突相互作用，后者在ALS UMN主导型样本的所有三个脊髓水平的侧向CST（侧向硬化）中出现，但未建立因果关系。
